attribution.note: The sentence is Zitron's own narration on his newsletter. The Business Insider material quoted after it is separate and is not the basis of the claim.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'appears' qualifier on both parts, performance and token use. Reading the predecessor as Opus 4.6 fits the preceding passage. This is a tentative observation, not a firm comparative finding.

contract.note: The contract correctly gives no binary support or contradiction condition, because 'appears to' is tentative. Treating the sentence as a claim of measured regression would strengthen the speaker's words.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure, dated 2026-04-16, before the cutoff. It says the new tokenizer can turn the same input into up to about 1.35x more tokens and that the model produces more output tokens at higher effort. It also claims net token usage improved and that benchmarks rose. This is company self-reporting and does not settle the tentative claim.

reviews.rationale: Zitron's claim is hedged with 'appears to', which policy treats as tentative or graded language that is not scored. The only evidence is an Anthropic disclosure. It partly fits the token concern because of the tokenizer change, but it also claims improvements. Either way, it cannot turn a tentative impression into a scorable claim. The outcome is not_adjudicable.
